chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Bus, ballrooms, theaters and repeat engagements on the coast tours
summary: They rented a bus, played ballrooms, theaters and hotels in San Francisco, Seattle and Vancouver.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How did you travel, by car? (Inaudible)?

No, we rented a bus. We rented a bus and a busdriver and he was with us constantly. We rented it from one of those kind of bus, like type of a sightseeing bus, and we rented it from one of the tour companies around town and he would go out and stay with us for a month or five, six weeks, however long we were out. We were never out much longer than after that.
Yes, almost completely ballrooms and with the exception of theaters -- we played theaters. Like,

we'd go to San Francisco and we would work the Golden Gate Theater for a week or two at a time and we would go to Seattle. We'd work the theater up there and when we went to Vancouver, we worked the theater in Vancouver. We'd work the theater for a week as well as working the dance hall in Vancouver and the same thing in Seattle.
B.C. And we worked hotels. Like, we worked the Winthrop Hotel and places like that up in Seattle.
And how long -- one-nighters and then -- a theater date was for longer, right?
Theater engagements would be for a week and when we worked hotels, it would be like weekly engagements, one or two weeks at a time.
Did you get more than a one-nighter from a ballroom or {inaudible}?

Ballrooms usually would consist of one night at a time. You may catch them going up toward -- going North, you might play them, and then may play them coming back down. If you were a big success going up, you were sure to play it coming down, because they would naturally want you and give you a little bit of raise in salary.
So how many tours like that did you make?
Everytime a big band would come in, we'd
probably go up once every couple of years or so, like Cab Calloway's band came in and played out there at the Cotton Club. Ellington's band came in --
